claim: A word pair can be turned into a count vector over mined joining-pattern types, and cosine between such vectors solves SAT analogies far above chance: VSM 47.1% recall (Turney and Littman 2005), LRA 56.1% (Turney 2006) vs chance 20% on 374 items.
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare an agent that retrieves analogues by an embedding of the relation (A:B pair text) against one that retrieves by surface similarity, on a held-out SAT/BATS-style set.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Relational similarity is not predicted by attributional (word-level) similarity: best WordNet and PMI word-similarity measures reach 28.5-35.0 F on SAT vs 47.4 for VSM and 56.5 for LRA.
agent_test: Check whether retrieving by topic similarity vs by relation description changes analogy-based solve rate at equal tokens.

claim: Two design choices carried the gain in LRA: learning 4,000 patterns from data (vs 64 fixed joining words) and thesaurus synonym expansion (recall 56.1 -> 49.5 without it, 22 skipped). SVD was not needed for accuracy (53.5 without, not significant).
agent_test: Ablate query rephrasing/expansion in analogy retrieval at equal tokens.

claim: Corpus size and cost are boundary conditions: the same VSM drops from 47.1% (5x10^11 words) to 38.5% (5x10^10 words, 34 skipped); LRA took almost nine days for 374 questions. Cheap vector methods needed web-scale text.
agent_test: Not applicable to a scaffold; an LLM already holds the corpus statistics.

claim: 'Human-level' for LRA is a statistical non-difference, not a win: 95% CI 51.0-61.2 contains 57%, and the human figure is estimated from a 78-item verbal test under an equal-difficulty assumption. The 190 official-test items scored 61.1% vs 51.1% on the other 184, so item source matters.
agent_test: Report binomial CIs for every analogy benchmark comparison; require n large enough to see a 5-point gap.

claim: The SAT is easy to beat with a prompted LLM: GPT-3 175B scored 53.7 zero-shot, 59.1 one-shot, 65.2 few-shot; ChatGPT zero-shot 74.8 and one-shot 83.7 (SCAR); fine-tuned RelBERT 69.5. Fewer in-context examples cost accuracy, and tuned LM scoring rivals LRA.
agent_test: Zero-shot vs one-shot vs few-shot analogy prompts at matched token budget on SAT/U2/U4.

claim: Vector-offset (a*-a+b) analogy accuracy is inflated by evaluation artifacts: with input words not excluded the nearest neighbour is b in 93% of cases; ONLY-B alone gets .70 on plurals; GloVe falls from 80.4% (Google) to 28.5% (BATS); LRCos reaches 47.7% on BATS.
schema_part: G (use baselines that ignore the relation)
agent_test: Always run an ONLY-B style baseline (answer from the target alone) next to any analogy-based method.

claim: Offset accuracy varies hugely by relation type and by pair frequency (Google categories 10.5%-99.4%; capitals 95.4% at median frequency 3,436 vs currencies 9.2% at frequency 19), so success on morphological and capital relations does not transfer to rare or lexical-semantic relations.
agent_test: Stratify any analogy test by relation frequency and type; report per stratum.

claim: Embedding cosine does not match human relational judgments on all relation types: it fails on SIMILAR, CONTRAST and NON-ATTRIBUTE relations and ignores presentation-order asymmetry (4.76 vs 2.36 for the same pair reversed).
agent_test: Test whether an LLM judge's relation similarity changes when pair order flips.

claim: A large share of strong LM analogy scores comes from answer-word artifacts: masking head or tail words of the candidate drops RoBERTa from 53.4 to 38.6/35.6 on SAT and from 93.6 to 60.6/55.8 on Google, yet stays above chance.
agent_test: Run a candidate-only (question hidden) control for any analogy benchmark we use.

claim: LLM analogy skill is brittle under counterfactual or perturbed forms: on permuted/symbol alphabets GPT models fall while humans barely change; story analogies show answer-order and paraphrase effects. Webb et al. (2023) report GPT-3 above humans on the standard forms.
agent_test: Evaluate our agent on original vs counterfactual variants at equal tokens.

claim: Self-generated analogous examples help modestly and depend on model strength: self-generated exemplars beat retrieved CoT by 4 points on text-davinci-003 GSM8K (61 vs 57) but are neutral or harmful on weak models (9 vs 11 on davinci-001); GPT-3.5-turbo 75.0 -> 77.8. (Gap search 2026: GPT-4 on Codeforces gains only +2 Acc@1 and +6 Acc@10 over 3-shot CoT; still no 2025-26 model tested.)
agent_test: Self-generated vs no-analogy prompts on GSM8K-style tasks at equal tokens, split by model size.

claim: External knowledge or noisy analogy data does not reliably help: unfiltered AnalogyKB samples had about 63% non-analogies and training on unchecked data hurt; KnowledgePrompts with structured knowledge reached 38-39% vs 45.7% zero-shot, with targeted knowledge best at 55.25%.
agent_test: Add a relevance filter to retrieved analogies and compare with unfiltered retrieval.

claim: Cheap similarity by text statistics is useful as a ranker, not as a final judge: top-1 over 369 candidates is only 8.4% (top-10 29.5%), but a margin threshold gives 59.2% precision at 11.2% recall. (Gap search 2026: a learned relation-informativeness score does separate easy from hard items, 31.1% to 71.2% average accuracy for RelBERT; the raw cosine margin for general LLM embeddings is still untested.)
agent_test: Use cosine margin between top candidate analogues to decide abstain/escalate at equal tokens.

claim: On the same SAT/U2/U4/BATS sets, a prompted GPT-4 (2023) scored SAT 70.3, U2 71.9, U4 68.8, BATS 90.8, Google 99.0, against RelBERT 73.6, 67.5, 63.0, 80.9, 81.4. A cheap fine-tuned relation-embedding model ties GPT-4 on SAT; GPT-4 wins on BATS/Google and on the hardest items.
agent_test: Use RelBERT-style scoring as the cheap baseline and a prompted model as the upper arm on SAT/U2/U4/BATS; report intervals.

claim: SAT, U2, U4 and BATS contamination for 2023-2025 models is unmeasured. The only memorisation probe (GPT-3, completion from A and B terms) found nothing; the benchmark authors themselves warn GPT-4 may have seen the items; letter-string tests with altered alphabets show 2023 GPT models drop where humans do not.
agent_test: Build perturbed copies (swap pairs, rename words, new relation wording) of any analogy test used to judge the agent.

claim: Relation-embedding confidence (min of the informativeness of query pair and chosen answer pair) predicts answer correctness: RelBERT average accuracy 31.1, 45.5, 58.7, 71.2 across four confidence bins over seven datasets; GPT-4 accuracy rises too (59.5 to 72.9).
agent_test: Test a confidence-gated fallback: cheap score for confident items, model call only below a threshold, at equal tokens.

claim: General sentence embeddings find similar things, not analogous things: on story pairs, RoBERTa, SimCSE and OpenAI-ada correlate 35-53 (x100) with entity and relation similarity but only 1.8-6.2 with the human analogy score; relation-aware models do better (DMR 12.6). Untrained BERT is near chance (0.47-0.52) at classifying word analogies and shows a word-frequency bias.
agent_test: Check a general embedding against a relation-aware or prompt-described embedding for retrieving analogous solved problems.

claim: When several relations are plausible, frontier LLMs (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, Llama3) choose the prototypical or embedding-nearest option and score about 22-36% on ranked relational overlap (chance 25%), against 44-53% on embedding similarity and prototypicality. Relation-asking prompts help weak models, not the best ones.
agent_test: When retrieving, state the relation wanted in the query; do not rely on the nearest prototype.

claim: Retrieval by shared method rather than shared topic is hard for embedding retrievers: on BRIGHT the best MTEB model drops from 59.0 to 18.3 nDCG@10; rewriting the query as an LLM reasoning trace raises retrieval by up to 12.2 points and makes BM25 on GPT-4 reasoning the top retriever. Similar-problem retrieval by cosine (Yasunaga's retrieved CoT) is beaten by self-generated analogues on strong models.
agent_test: Equal-token test: topic embedding vs model-written relation description as the retrieval query, on held-out solved problems.

claim: Rare, new relations lower LLM analogy scores: ChatGPT-4o-mini and Llama 3 8B score about 80-87 on English BATS but about 50-60 on 2,600 fine-grained French lexical analogies (ALF), and sentence-pair cosine is biased by word frequency. The size of memorisation in this gap is not separated from language and relation type.
agent_test: Evaluate the agent on domain relations that are rare in public text (code idioms, lab methods), not on SAT-style pairs.
